blocks.title: A local, family-run school built on passion.
body: Welcome to Mauritius! Born To Kite is a local, family-run school founded in January 2026. I have taught kitesurfing for more than ten years, and my goal is simple: to share my passion with patience, a friendly atmosphere and the highest possible level of safety.
Escape into the turquoise waters of Mauritius, discover an exciting sport and enjoy an experience shaped around you.
We are based in the south of Mauritius, mainly on Le Morne lagoon. Depending on the weather, we can move to another spot in the area to give you the best possible conditions.

items.q: What level do I need to start kitesurfing?
items.a: No previous experience is required. Lessons begin with theory and kite handling on land before entering the water. You must be able to swim.

items.q: How long does it take to ride independently?
items.a: In general, 6 to 10 hours of lessons are enough to learn the basics of riding independently, depending on your confidence and the wind conditions.
Yes. The kite, board, harness, helmet and buoyancy aid are all included and selected for your size and the day's wind.

The easiest way is to send us your availability on WhatsApp. We confirm the time according to the weather.

pages.title: Le Morne spot: wind, seasons and safety
pages.description: A guide to Le Morne lagoon: prevailing wind, trade-wind season, flat water protected by the coral reef and right-of-way rules on the water.

blocks.title: A lagoon shaped by volcano and coral.
body: Mauritius was formed by volcanic activity around 8 million years ago. Today, an almost continuous coral reef surrounds the island, creating a shallow lagoon protected from the large Indian Ocean swells and providing an ideal setting for learning to kitesurf safely.

Le Morne, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, owes its dramatic landscape to this volcanic origin. Its peninsula creates a stretch of water that is both windy and sheltered, unlike anywhere else on the island.

Coral reefs are a fragile ecosystem. They support much of Mauritius' marine life and protect the coastline from erosion. When riding, we stay over sandy areas and make sure the equipment never touches the coral.

blocks.alt: Le Morne and its lagoon seen from the air, Mauritius

blocks.title: The wind
body: At Le Morne, the prevailing south-easterly trade wind is generally stronger in the early afternoon. Our instructors check the conditions before every session and choose equipment suited to the wind strength and your level.
Le Morne lagoon is protected by the coral reef. The water is flat and free from large waves, making it an ideal place to learn.

items.title: The wind
items.body: At Le Morne, the prevailing south-easterly trade wind is generally stronger in the early afternoon.

items.title: The waves
items.body: The inside of the lagoon remains flat. Surfable waves are found offshore beyond the reef, with coaching adapted to each person's level.

items.title: Safety
items.body: You must be able to swim. Give way to the surfer already riding the wave and keep a safe distance from other water users.

blocks.lead: Conditions observed by the school to help you choose the period best suited to your level. These figures are for kitesurfing: wingfoiling needs fewer knots.

blocks.title: Choosing when to visit.
body: The wind generally blows from 7:00 am to 6:30 pm and is stronger in the early afternoon. It also depends on the tide and increases as the tide rises.
From November to April, the school adapts to the conditions. If there is not enough wind, the session is refunded or rescheduled, or we may move to another spot.
February is the least reliable month for kitesurfing. December and mid-January are also less consistent, although nature always remains unpredictable.
The lagoon is busier from May to September and starts to become quieter from late September.

blocks.alt: Kitesurf kites on Le Morne beach beneath a rainbow, Mauritius
blocks.caption: The launch area on the lagoon side.

items.a: The rider who is downwind always has priority.
Never pass between a rider and their kite or over their lines.
If in doubt, slow down and give way.

body: Website publisher: Born To Kite, Ritik Jouan, Beachfront Kitelagoon, Le Morne, Rivière Noire, Mauritius. Contact: contact@borntokitemauritius.com or +230 5487 9629.
The website is hosted on Cloudflare Pages and uses the domain borntokitemauritius.com.

The website does not create user accounts or collect data through a form. WhatsApp and email links open the services selected by the visitor. The Windguru module uses deferred loading: when it loads, the browser connects to Windguru, which may receive technical data such as the IP address.

For questions about your personal data or to exercise your rights of access and rectification, email contact@borntokitemauritius.com. Personal data processing in Mauritius is governed by the Data Protection Act 2017.
